If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
190.sol: Polytene chromosomes are quite common in salivary glands of insects and so are called salivary chromosomes. These chromosomes have high amount of DNA of almost 1000 times in Drosophila as compared to ordinary somatic chromosomes. These chromosomes are multistranded. They are in permanent prophase stage. These chromosomese are formed by somatic pairing between homologous chromosomes and repeated replication of their chromonemata without separation of chromatids. All the chromosomes may remain attached to one another at a common point called chromocentre.

1500.text: Suppose the gravitational force varies inversely as the \(n^{\text{th }}\) power of distance. Then the time period of a planet in circular orbit of radius \(R\) around the sun will be proportional to
1500.sol:
Gravitational force, $F \propto \frac{1}{r^n} F=\frac{k}{r^n}$ where $k$ is a constant.
For a planet, moving in a circular orbit of radius $R, F=\frac{k}{R^n}$
But, $F=m \omega^2 R \begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{k}{R^n}=m R \cdot\left(\frac{2 \pi}{T}\right)^2 \Rightarrow \frac{k}{R^{n+1}}=\frac{m(2 \pi)^2}{T^2} \\ & \Rightarrow T^2 \propto R^{n+1} \\ & \therefore T \propto R^{\frac{n+1}{2}} .\end{aligned}$

2094.subject: Zoology
2094.text: Which of the following is true regarding sperm?
2094.sol: Hyaluronidase is a hydrolytic enzyme present in the acrosome of sperm (human testes). It lyses the glycosaminoglycans in the extracellular matrix holding the cell of the corona radiata together. As the coronal cells become more loosely associated, sperm cells can propel themselves inward, toward the zona pellucida by making a receptive cone or fertilization cone through the cytoplasm of the egg. Hyaluronidase may also be involved in breaking down the Zona Pellucida. Fertilizin is a chemical substance secreted from the cortical region of egg cytoplasm to attract the sperm towards the egg. Acrosin is released from the acrosome of a spermatozoa as a consequence of the acrosome reaction. It aids in the penetration of Zona Pellucida. Capacitation is the final stage in the maturation process of spermatozoa. This takes place inside the genital tract as the sperm penetrates the ovum.

4889.text: Which of the following represents the correct order for oxidising power of the given species $\mathrm{ClO}_4^{-}, \mathrm{BrO}_4^{-}$ and $\mathrm{IO}_4^{-}$?
4889.sol:
The reduction potential of the substance is the ability of the substance to be reduced. So, as the reduction potential increases, reducing ability of substance increases.
It means oxidising power of the substance increases. The ability of the substance to make the other substance to lose the electrons increase.
So, order of oxidising power is $\mathrm{BrO}_4^{-} > \mathrm{IO}_4^{-} > \mathrm{ClO}_4^{-}$.

5436.text: If $100 \mathrm{ L}$ of an ideal gas at a pressure of $2 \mathrm{ atm}$ compressed isothermally and reversibly to a final volume of ' $\mathrm{X}$ ' $\mathrm{L}$ releases $-460.6 \mathrm{ L} \mathrm{ atm}$ heat, the final volume ' $\mathrm{X}$ ' (in $\mathrm{L}$ ) is
5436.sol:
$\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{w}=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{w}=-\mathrm{q}$
We have, $\mathrm{q}=-460.6 \mathrm{ L} \mathrm{ atm}\Rightarrow \mathrm{w}=+460.6 \mathrm{ L} \mathrm{ atm}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{W}=-2.303 \mathrm{nRT} \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_2}{\mathrm{ V}_1}\right) \\
& =-2.303\left(\mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{ V}_1\right) \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_2}{\mathrm{ V}_1}\right) \\
& =-2.303(2 \times 100) \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_2}{100}\right) \\
& =-460.6\left[\log \left(\mathrm{V}_2\right)-\log (100)\right] \\
& -460.6\left[\log \left(\mathrm{V}_2\right)-2\right]=921.2-460.6 \log \left(\mathrm{V}_2\right)=460.6 \\
& \Rightarrow \log \left(\mathrm{V}_2\right)=\frac{921.2-460.6}{460.6}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_2=10 \mathrm{ L}(\mathrm{X})
\end{aligned}$

Since, $f(x)$ attain local minimum and maximum at $x=-2 and x=2$ respectively.
$\therefore f^{\prime}(x)=k(x+2)(x-2)=k \left(x^2-4\right) ...(ii)$ From (i) and (ii)\begin{aligned} & k$\left(x^2-4\right)$=3 p x^2+2 q x+r \\ & \Rightarrow \quad k x^2-4 k=3 p x^2+2 q x+r\end{aligned}$

19781.subject: Chemistry
19781.text:
Which of these molecules have non-bonding electron pairs on the cental atom?
$\mathrm{I}: \mathrm{SF}_4 : \mathrm{II}: \mathrm{ICl}_3 : \mathrm{III}: \mathrm{SO}_2$
19781.sol:
For $\mathrm{SF}_4$, the central atom is sulfur (group 16). Sulfur has 6 valence electrons. It forms 4 bonds with fluorine atoms, leaving $6 - 4 = 2$ electrons, which corresponds to 1 lone pair on the sulfur atom.

For $\mathrm{ICl}_3$, the central atom is iodine (group 17). Iodine has 7 valence electrons. It forms 3 bonds with chlorine atoms, leaving $7 - 3 = 4$ electrons, which corresponds to 2 lone pairs on the iodine atom.

For $\mathrm{SO}_2$, the central atom is sulfur (group 16). Sulfur has 6 valence electrons. It forms 2 double bonds with oxygen atoms (total 4 electrons used for bonding), leaving $6 - 4 = 2$ electrons, which corresponds to 1 lone pair on the sulfur atom.

Since all three molecules $\mathrm{SF}_4$, $\mathrm{ICl}_3$, and $\mathrm{SO}_2$ possess non-bonding electron pairs on their respective central atoms, the correct option is I, II and III.

Answer: I, II and III

$[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}]^{3} = \dfrac{0.5}{4} = 0.125$

$[\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{2}] = (0.125)^{1/3} = (0.5^{3})^{1/3} = 0.5 \mathrm{ mol} \mathrm{ L}^{-1}$.

20845.text:
The enthalpy change accompanying the freezing of 18 g of water at $5^{{}^{\circ}} $$\mathrm{C}$$ to ice at $-5^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}$ is:
[Given: $\Delta H_{(\text{fusion })}=6 \mathrm{ kJ} $$\mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ at $0^{{}^{\circ}} $\mathrm{C}$ ; \quad C_p$\left(H_2 $\mathrm{O}$, l\right)$=75.3 $\mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ K}^{-1} $\mathrm{ mol}^{-1} ; \quad C_p$\left(H_2 $\mathrm{O}$, s\right)$=36.8 $\mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ K}^{-1} $\mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$$ ]$
20845.sol:
The process of freezing 18 g (1 mole) of water at $5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to ice at $-5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ can be broken down into three steps:

Cooling 1 mole of liquid water from $5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to $0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$.
$\Delta H_1 = n C_p(l) \Delta T = 1 \times 75.3 \times (0 - 5) \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ kJ} = -0.3765 \mathrm{ kJ}$

Phase change of 1 mole of liquid water at $0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to ice at $0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$.
$\Delta H_2 = -\Delta H_{\text{fusion}} = -6.0 \mathrm{ kJ}$

Cooling 1 mole of ice from $0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to $-5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$.
$\Delta H_3 = n C_p(s) \Delta T = 1 \times 36.8 \times (-5 - 0) \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ kJ} = -0.184 \mathrm{ kJ}$

Total enthalpy change $\Delta H = \Delta H_1 + \Delta H_2 + \Delta H_3 = -0.3765 - 6.0 - 0.184 = -6.5605 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $-6.56 \mathrm{ kJ} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$

21003.subject: Mathematics
21003.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^2=2 y-x$ and the $y$-axis is
21003.sol:
The given equation of the curve is $y^2 = 2y - x$, which can be rewritten as $x = 2y - y^2$.

The curve intersects the $y$-axis where $x = 0$. Setting $x = 0$ in the equation $x = 2y - y^2$, we get $2y - y^2 = 0$, which implies $y(2 - y) = 0$. Thus, the points of intersection are $y = 0$ and $y = 2$.

The area $A$ of the region bounded by the curve and the $y$-axis is given by the integral of $x$ with respect to $y$ from $y = 0$ to $y = 2$.

$A = \int_{0}^{2} (2y - y^2) dy$

Evaluating the integral:

$A = \left[ y^2 - \dfrac{y^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$A = \left( 2^2 - \dfrac{2^3}{3} \right) - (0 - 0)$

$A = 4 - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{12 - 8}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ sq units.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$ sq units

21646.subject: Mathematics
21646.sol:
Given the limit $L = \lim _{x \rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{4}} \dfrac{\sec ^2 x-2}{\tan x-1}$.

Using the identity $\sec ^2 x = 1 + \tan ^2 x$, the expression becomes:

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{4}} \dfrac{1 + \tan ^2 x - 2}{\tan x - 1}$

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{4}} \dfrac{\tan ^2 x - 1}{\tan x - 1}$

Factoring the numerator as a difference of squares:

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{4}} \dfrac{(\tan x - 1)(\tan x + 1)}{\tan x - 1}$

Canceling the common term $(\tan x - 1)$ for $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$L = \lim _{x \rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{4}} (\tan x + 1)$

Substituting $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$L = \tan \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2$.

Answer: 2

26686.text:
One mole of a monatomic ideal gas undergoes four thermodynamic processes as shown schematically in the PV - diagram below. Among these four processes, one is isobaric, one is isochoric, one is isothermal and one is adiabatic. Match the processes mentioned in List-1 with the corresponding statements in List-II.

 LIST -I LIST -II

B)In process $II$Q)Temperature of the gas remains unchanged

26686.sol:
Process - $I$ is an adiabatic process
$∆ Q = ∆ U + W$
$∆ Q = 0$
$W = - ∆ U$
Volume of gas is decreasing $⇒ W < 0$
$∆ U > 0$
$⇒$ Temperatuer of gas increases
$⇒$ No heat is exchanged between the gas and surrounding.
Process - $II$ is an isobaric process
(Pressure remain constant)
$W = P ∆ V = 3{P}_{0}\left[3{V}_{0} - {V}_{0}\right] = 6{P}_{0}{V}_{0}$
Process - $III$ is an isochoric process
(Volume remain constant)
$∆ Q = ∆ U + W$
$W = 0$
$∆ Q = ∆ U$
Process - $IV$ is an isothermal process
(Temperature remains constant)
$∆ Q = ∆ U + W$
$∆ U = 0$

33072.subject: Mathematics
33072.text: The area of the region $\{(x, y) : 0 \leq y \leq 6 - x, y^2 \geq 4x - 3, x \geq 0\}$ is:
33072.sol:
The given region is defined by the inequalities:
$x \geq 0$
$0 \leq y \leq 6 - x \Rightarrow y \geq 0$ and $x \leq 6 - y$
$y^2 \geq 4x - 3 \Rightarrow x \leq \dfrac{y^2 + 3}{4}$

From these inequalities, for a given $y \geq 0$, the value of $x$ ranges from $0$ to $\min\left(6 - y, \dfrac{y^2 + 3}{4}\right)$.

To find the point where the two bounding curves intersect, we equate them:
$6 - y = \dfrac{y^2 + 3}{4}$

$24 - 4y = y^2 + 3$

$y^2 + 4y - 21 = 0$

$(y + 7)(y - 3) = 0$

Since $y \geq 0$, the intersection occurs at $y = 3$.

For $0 \leq y \leq 3$, the right boundary is the parabola $x = \dfrac{y^2 + 3}{4}$.
For $3 \leq y \leq 6$, the right boundary is the line $x = 6 - y$.

The total area $A$ can be calculated by integrating with respect to $y$:
$A = \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{y^2 + 3}{4} dy + \int_{3}^{6} (6 - y) dy$

Evaluating the first integral:
$\int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{y^2 + 3}{4} dy = \dfrac{1}{4} \left[ \dfrac{y^3}{3} + 3y \right]_{0}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{4} (9 + 9) = \dfrac{18}{4} = \dfrac{9}{2}$

Evaluating the second integral:
$\int_{3}^{6} (6 - y) dy = \left[ 6y - \dfrac{y^2}{2} \right]_{3}^{6} = (36 - 18) - \left(18 - \dfrac{9}{2}\right) = 18 - 13.5 = \dfrac{9}{2}$

Total Area = $\dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} = 9$

Answer: $9$

33719.text:
Given : A circle, $2{x}^{2} + 2{y}^{2} = 5$ and a parabola, ${y}^{2} = 4\sqrt{5}x$.

Statement - I : An equation of a common tangent to these curves is $y = x + \sqrt{5}$.

Statement - II : If the line, $y = mx + \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{m}\left(m \ne 0\right)$ is their common tangent, then $m$ satisfies ${m}^{4} - 3{m}^{2} + 2 = 0$.
options: Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is false.
Statement - $I$ is false; Statement - $II$ is true.
Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is a correct explanation for statement - $I$.
Statement - $I$ is true; Statement - $II$ is true; Statement - $II$ is not a correct explanation for statement - $I$.
33719.sol:
Tangent to ${y}^{2} = 4\sqrt{5}x$ will be $y = mx + \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{m}$
As tangent to ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{2}$ will be $y = mx \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{1 + {m}^{2}}$
Hence for common tangent

$\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{m} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{1 + {m}^{2}}$
$⇒ {m}^{4} + {m}^{2} - 2 = 0$

$⇒ {m}^{2} = 1$ , ${m}^{2} = - 2$ (Not Possible)

$⇒ m = \pm 1$
Hence common tangent is $y = x + \sqrt{5}$

Both the statements are correct

The values of $m$ also satisfy the equation in statement - $II$ but it is not a correct explanation for statement - $I$.

35428.sol:
We have,

$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1 . . . \left(i\right)$

On differentiating w.r.t., $x,$ we get

$\dfrac{2x}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{2y}{{b}^{2}} \times \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)$

$⇒ - \dfrac{dx}{dy} = - \dfrac{{a}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)$

Slope for normal at the point $P\left(asec\theta, btan\theta\right)$ is

${\left(- \dfrac{dx}{dy}\right)}_{P} = - \dfrac{{a}^{2}btan\theta}{{b}^{2}asec\theta} = - \dfrac{a}{b}sin\theta$

$∴$ Equation of normal at $\left(asec\theta, btan\theta\right)$ is

$y - btan\theta = - \dfrac{a}{b}sin\theta\left(x - asec\theta\right)$

$⇒ \left(asin\theta\right)x + by = \left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)tan\theta$

$⇒ ax + b cosec \thetay = \left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)sec\theta . . . \left(ii\right)$

Similarly, equation of normal to $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ at

$( asecϕ, btanϕ )$ is

$ax + by cosec ϕ = \left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)secϕ . . . \left(ii\right)$

On subtracting $\left(ii\right)$ from $\left(i\right)$, we get

$b ( cosec \theta - cosec ϕ ) y = \left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right) ( sec\theta - secϕ )$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}{b} \cdot \left(\dfrac{sec\theta - secϕ}{cosec \theta - cosec ϕ}\right)$

But $\dfrac{sec\theta - secϕ}{cosec \theta - cosec ϕ} = \dfrac{sec\theta - sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)}{cosec \theta - cosec \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)}$

$\left[∵ ϕ + \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$= \dfrac{sec\theta - cosec \theta}{cosec\theta - sec\theta} = - 1$

Thus,

$y = - \left(\dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}{b}\right),$ i.e., $k = 2$.

36324.subject: Mathematics
36324.text: A person has three different bags and four different books. The number of ways, in which he can put these books in the bags so that no bag is empty, is:
36324.sol:
To ensure no bag is empty, exactly one bag must contain 2 books and the other two bags must contain 1 book each.

The number of ways to choose 2 books out of 4 to be kept together is $^{4}C_{2} = 6$

Now, we have 3 units (one pair of books and two single books) to be distributed into the 3 different bags.

The number of ways to distribute these 3 units into 3 bags is $3! = 6$

Total number of ways = $6 \times 6 = 36$

Answer: $36$

38193.text: Let $S$ be the set of all real values of $\lambda$ such that a plane passing through the points $\left(- {\lambda}^{2}, 1, 1\right), \left(1, - {\lambda}^{2}, 1\right) and \left(1, 1, - {\lambda}^{2}\right) also passes through the point \left(- 1, - 1, 1\right). Then $S$ is equal to :$

As we know that if four points $P, A, B, C$ are coplanar, the vectors $\overset{\to}{PA}, \overset{\to}{PB}, \overset{\to}{PC}$ must be coplanar.

$⇒ \left(- {\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left({\lambda}^{4} - 1\right) + 4\left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(- {\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left({\lambda}^{2} - 1\right) + 4\left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left\{\left(- {\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left({\lambda}^{2} - 1\right) + 4\right\} = 0$

$⇒ - \left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left({\lambda}^{4} - 2{\lambda}^{2} + 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ - \left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right)\left({\lambda}^{2} - 3\right)\left({\lambda}^{2} + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm \sqrt{3}$

39060.text: An electron in a hydrogen atom makes a transition from $n = 2$ to $n = 1$ and emits a photon. Let us assume that the electron in the lithium-ion is knocked off from the ${n}^{th}$ energy level, then

$R{\left({Z}_{H}\right)}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{{1}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}}\right) = R\dfrac{{\left({Z}_{Li}\right)}^{2}}{{n}^{2}}$

$R{\left(1\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{3}{4} = R{\left(3\right)}^{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}\right]$

$\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{9}{{n}^{2}}$

$n = \sqrt{12} \approx 3 . 5$

Hence the least quantum number must be $4$.

40523.text: Two charges of $- 4\mu C$ and $+ 4\mu C$ are placed at the points $A ( 1, 0, 4 ) m$ and $B ( 2, - 1, 5 ) m$ located in an electric field $\overset{\to}{E} = 0 . 20\overset{^}{i}V{cm}^{- 1}$. The magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole is $8\sqrt{\alpha} \times {10}^{- 5}Nm$, where $\alpha =$_________.
40523.sol:
Given the electric field is

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{E} & = & 0 . 20\overset{^}{i}\dfrac{V}{cm} \\ & = & 20\overset{^}{i}\dfrac{V}{m}\end{cases}$

The formula for calculating the torque is

$\overset{\to}{τ} = \overset{\to}{p} \times \overset{\to}{E} . . . \left(1\right)$

where,

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{p} & = & q\overset{\to}{l} \\ & = & 4 \times \left[\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \left(- 1\right)\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(1\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}\right)\right] \\ & = & 4\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\mu Cm\end{cases}$

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

$\overset{\to}{τ} = ( 4\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} ) \times {10}^{- 6} \times ( 20\overset{^}{i} ) Nm = ( 8\overset{^}{k} + 8\overset{^}{j} ) \times {10}^{- 5}Nm ⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{τ}\right| = \sqrt{{8}^{2} + {8}^{2}} \times {10}^{- 5}Nm = 8\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 5}Nm$

Hence, $\alpha = 2$.

42567.text: A sample contains ${10}^{- 2}kg$ each of two substances $A$ and $B$ with half lives $4s$ and $8s$ respectively. The ratio of their atomic weights is $1: 2$. The ratio of the amounts of $A$ and $B$ after $16s$ is $\dfrac{x}{100}$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
42567.sol:
Ratio of number of moles of substance in the beginning will be, $\dfrac{{\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{A}}{{\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{B}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{10}^{- 2}kg}{{M}_{A}}}{\dfrac{{10}^{- 2}kg}{{M}_{B}}} = \dfrac{{M}_{B}}{{M}_{A}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Number of half-life in $16s$ for element $A$ will be, ${n}_{A} = \dfrac{16}{4} = 4$

Number of half-life in $16s$ for element $B$ will be, ${n}_{B} = \dfrac{16}{8} = 2$

Hence, ratio of number of nuclei after $16s$ will be, $= \dfrac{{\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{A} \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{{n}_{A}}}{{\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{B} \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{{n}_{B}}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{4 - 2} = \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{25}{100}$

Thus, value of $x$ is $25$.

42619.subject: Physics
42619.text: A radioactive nuclei with decay constant $0.5 / \mathrm{s}$ is being produced at a constant rate of 100 nuclei/s. If at $t=0$ there were no nuclei, the time when there are 50 nuclei is:
42619.sol:
Let $N$ be the number of nuclei at any time $t$ then,

$\begin{aligned} \frac{d N}{d t}=$100-\lambda N \\
 $\text{$ or $} \int_$0^N $\frac{d N}{(100-\lambda N)}=\int_$0^t d t \\
&-$\frac{1}{\lambda}[\log (100-\lambda N)]_0^N=t \\
&\log (100-\lambda N)-\log 100=-\lambda t \\
&\log \frac{100-\lambda N}{100}=-\lambda$ t \\
 $\frac{100-\lambda N}{100}=$ e^{-\lambda t} \\
&1-$\frac{\lambda N}{100}=$ e^{-\lambda t}
\end{aligned}

$\begin{aligned}$&N=$\frac{100}{\lambda}\left(1-e^{-\lambda} t\right) \\
 \text{ As, }$ N=50 $\text{$ and $} \lambda=$0.5 / $\mathrm\sec\\
&\therefore 50=\frac{100}{0.5}\left(1-e^{-0.5 t}\right)
\end{aligned}

Solving we get,

t=2 \ln \left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \mathrm\sec$

47668.subject: Chemistry
47668.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: The $\text{M}-\text{C}\sigma$ bond is formed by the donation of lone pair of electrons on the carbonyl carbon into a vacant d-orbital of the metal.
Statement-II: The $\text{M}-\text{C}\pi$ bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from a filled d-orbital of metal into the vacant antibonding $\pi^*$ orbital of carbon monoxide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
47668.sol:
According to the bonding in metal carbonyls:

Statement-I is incorrect because the $\text{M}-\text{C}\sigma$ bond is formed by the donation of a lone pair of electrons from the carbonyl carbon into a vacant hybrid orbital of the metal, not necessarily a vacant d-orbital. For example, in $\text{Ni(CO)}_4$, the nickel atom is $sp^3$ hybridized (3d^{10}$ configuration) and the \sigma$ bonds are formed by donation into vacant $sp^3$ hybrid orbitals, with no vacant d-orbitals involved.

Statement-II is correct because the $\text{M}-\text{C}\pi$ bond is formed by the back-donation of a pair of electrons from a filled d-orbital of the metal into the vacant antibonding $\pi^{*}$ orbital of carbon monoxide. This is known as synergic bonding.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

According to the rules of reflection for spherical mirrors, an incident ray parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror passes through its principal focus ($F$) after reflection.

Among the given rays, ray $C$ passes through the principal focus $F$.

Thus, ray $C$ correctly shows the direction of the reflected ray.

Answer: C

54852.subject: Chemistry
54852.text: Which of the following ether, on hydrolysis, gives two different products that are successive members of the homologous series?
54852.sol:
Hydrolysis of an ether $R-O-R'$ yields two alcohol molecules, $R-OH$ and $R'-OH$.

For the products to be successive members of a homologous series, they must differ by exactly one $-CH_2-$ unit. This means the alkyl groups $R$ and $R'$ must differ by one carbon atom.

Methoxymethane (CH_3-O-CH_3$) gives two molecules of methanol, which are identical.

Methoxypropane (CH_3-O-C_3H_7$) gives methanol and propanol, which differ by two carbon atoms.

Ethoxypropane (C_2H_5-O-C_3H_7$) gives ethanol (C_2H_5OH$) and propanol (C_3H_7OH$). These are successive members of the alcohol homologous series as they differ by one $-CH_2-$ group.

Answer: Ethoxypropane$

56446.subject: Chemistry
56446.text: Identify the correct increasing order of field strength of ligands form following.
56446.sol:
The spectrochemical series ranks ligands by crystal field splitting strength $\Delta$. The general increasing order for common ligands is:

$\mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{Br}^{-} < \mathrm{S}^{2-} < \mathrm{SCN}^{-} \text{ (S-bonded)} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-} < \mathrm{F}^{-} < \mathrm{OH}^{-} < \mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} < \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} < \mathrm{NCS}^{-} \text{ (N-bonded)} < \mathrm{EDTA}^{4-} < \mathrm{NH}_{3} < \mathrm{en} < \mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-} < \mathrm{PPh}_{3} < \mathrm{CN}^{-} < \mathrm{CO}$

Among the given ligands, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is the weakest due to its large size and strong $\pi$-donation, while $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ is the strongest owing to oxygen's high electronegativity and effective $\sigma$-donation. Chloride $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is stronger than iodide but weaker than hydroxide. Sulfide $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$, with its higher charge, typically exhibits intermediate strength.

Comparing the options:

A) $\mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{S}^{2-} < \mathrm{OH}^{-}$ is invalid since $\mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$.
B) $\mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{S}^{2-} < \mathrm{OH}^{-}$ correctly starts with the weakest and ends with the strongest ligand.
C) $\mathrm{OH}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{S}^{2-}$ incorrectly positions $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ as weakest.
D) $\mathrm{S}^{2-} < \mathrm{OH}^{-} < \mathrm{I}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is invalid due to multiple misorderings.

The only valid increasing order is B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

56808.subject: Chemistry
56808.text:
If standard reduction potential of Zn, Ni and Fe are $-0.76\,\text{V}$, $-0.23\,\text{V}$ and $-0.44\,\text{V}$ respectively. For the reaction (Stated below) to be spontaneous find out electrodes X and Y considering above electrode potentials
$\text{X}_{(s)} + \textY^{+2}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \textX^{+2}_{(aq)} + \text{Y}_{(s)}$
56808.sol:
For the given reaction $\text{X}_{(s)} + \textY^{+2}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow \textX^{+2}_{(aq)} + \text{Y}_{(s)}$, X undergoes oxidation and acts as the anode, while Y undergoes reduction and acts as the cathode.

For the reaction to be spontaneous, the standard cell potential $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}}$ must be positive.

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{anode}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Y}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{X}} > 0$

This implies $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Y}} > E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{X}}$.

Given standard reduction potentials:
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Zn}} = -0.76\,\text{V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Ni}} = -0.23\,\text{V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{Fe}} = -0.44\,\text{V}$

Checking the given options:
If X = Ni, Y = Fe: $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.44 - (-0.23) = -0.21\,\text{V}$ (Non-spontaneous)
If X = Ni, Y = Zn: $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.76 - (-0.23) = -0.53\,\text{V}$ (Non-spontaneous)
If X = Fe, Y = Zn: $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.76 - (-0.44) = -0.32\,\text{V}$ (Non-spontaneous)
If X = Zn, Y = Ni: $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.23 - (-0.76) = +0.53\,\text{V}$ (Spontaneous)

Thus, the reaction is spontaneous when X = Zn and Y = Ni.

Answer: X = Zn , Y = Ni

60215.subject: Mathematics
60215.text: The surface area of a spherical ball is increasing at the rate of $4\pi\ \text{cm}^2$/second. The rate at which the radius is increasing when the surface area is $16\pi\ \text{cm}^2$ is
60215.sol:
Let $S$ be the surface area and $r$ be the radius of the spherical ball.

$S = 4\pi r^2$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 8\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

Given $\dfrac{dS}{dt} = 4\pi$ cm^2$/s.

When $S = 16\pi$ cm^2$:

$4\pi r^2 = 16\pi \Rightarrow r^2 = 4 \Rightarrow r = 2$ cm.

Substituting the values into the derivative equation:

$4\pi = 8\pi (2) \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

$4\pi = 16\pi \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{4\pi}{16\pi} = 0.25$ cm/s.

60575.subject: Mathematics
60575.text: The area bounded by the curve $y = x\left|\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right|$ and the X-axis between the lines $x = 0$ and $x = 4\pi$ (in square units), is....
60575.sol:
The required area is given by the integral:

$A = \int_{0}^{4\pi} x\left|\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right| dx$

Since $\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \ge 0$ for $x \in [0, 2\pi]$ and $\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \le 0$ for $x \in [2\pi, 4\pi]$, the integral can be split as:

$A = \int_{0}^{2\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx - \int_{2\pi}^{4\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx$

Using integration by parts:

$\int x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx = x\left(-2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right) - \int 1 \cdot \left(-2\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right) dx$

$= -2x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{0}^{2\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx = \left[-2x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{0}^{2\pi} = (-4\pi(-1) + 0) - (0 + 0) = 4\pi$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{2\pi}^{4\pi} x\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx = \left[-2x\cos\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 4\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{2\pi}^{4\pi} = (-8\pi(1) + 0) - (-4\pi(-1) + 0) = -8\pi - 4\pi = -12\pi$

Substituting these values back into the area expression:

$A = 4\pi - (-12\pi) = 16\pi$

Answer: $16\pi$

60589.subject: Mathematics
60589.text: The area inside the parabola $y^2=4 a x$, between the lines $x=a$ and $x=4 a$ is equal to
60589.sol:
Area inside the parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ between $x = a$ and $x = 4a$.

The parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ is symmetric about the x-axis, with the upper half given by $y = 2\sqrt{ax}$.

The total area is twice the area above the x-axis, so we compute $A = 2 \int_a^{4a} 2\sqrt{ax} dx = 4\sqrt{a} \int_a^{4a} \sqrt{x} dx$.

Evaluating the integral: $4\sqrt{a} \left[ \frac{2}{3} x^{3/2} \right]_a^{4a} = \frac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} \left( (4a)^{3/2} - a^{3/2} \right)$.

Simplifying: $(4a)^{3/2} = 8a^{3/2}$, so $A = \frac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} (8a^{3/2} - a^{3/2}) = \frac{8\sqrt{a}}{3} \cdot 7a^{3/2} = \frac{56}{3} a^2$.

This corresponds to option C: $\frac{56a^2}{3}$ square units.

61349.subject: Mathematics
61349.text: The assets of a person reduced in his business such that the rate of reduction is proportional to the square root of the existing assets. If the assets were initially ₹ 10 lakhs and due to loss they reduce to $₹ 10000$ after 3 years, then the number of years required for the person to be bankrupt will be
61349.sol:
If $A$ denotes the assets at time $t$, the rate of reduction is proportional to $\sqrt{A}, so

\frac{dA}{dt} = -k\sqrt{A}$

Separating and integrating gives

$\int A^{-1/2}\,dA = \int -k\,dt$

$2\sqrt{A} = -kt + C$

At $t = 0$, $A = 10^6$, hence $2\sqrt{10^6} = C$, so $C = 2000$.

At $t = 3$, $A = 10^4$, giving $2\sqrt{10^4} = -3k + 2000$
$200 = -3k + 2000$
$k = 600$

The solution becomes $2\sqrt{A} = -600t + 2000$.
Set $A = 0$ for bankruptcy: $0 = -600t + 2000$, so $t = \frac{2000}{600} = \frac{10}{3}$ years.

Correct choice is B.

65091.subject: Mathematics
65091.text: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram ABCD are given by $\overline{AB} = 2\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$ and $\overline{AD} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. The side AD is rotated by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that AD becomes AD'. If AD' makes a right angle with the side AB, then the cosine of the angle $\alpha$ is given by
65091.sol:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$.

Using the dot product formula, we have:
$\cos \theta = \dfrac{\overrightarrow{AB} \cdot \overrightarrow{AD}}{|\overrightarrow{AB}| |\overrightarrow{AD}|}$

Given $\overrightarrow{AB} = 2\hat{i} + 10\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, we calculate the dot product:
$\overrightarrow{AB} \cdot \overrightarrow{AD} = (2)(-1) + (10)(2) + (11)(2) = -2 + 20 + 22 = 40$

Now, we find the magnitudes of the vectors:
$|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 10^2 + 11^2} = \sqrt{4 + 100 + 121} = \sqrt{225} = 15$
$|\overrightarrow{AD}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{9} = 3$

Substituting these values into the cosine formula:
$\cos \theta = \dfrac{40}{15 \times 3} = \dfrac{40}{45} = \dfrac{8}{9}$

Since $\cos \theta > 0$, the angle $\theta$ is acute. The side AD is rotated by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram to become AD', which is perpendicular to AB. This means the angle between AB and AD' is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Since both $\theta$ and $\alpha$ are acute, the rotation must satisfy:
$\theta + \alpha = 90^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow \alpha = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta$

We need to find $\cos \alpha$:
$\cos \alpha = \cos(90^{{}^{\circ}} - \theta) = \sin \theta$

Using the identity $\sin \theta = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2 \theta}$:
$\cos \alpha = \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right)^2} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{81}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{17}{81}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$

67023.subject: Physics
67023.text:
Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?
a. Work done to move a charge on an equipotential surface is not zero.
b. Equipotential surfaces are the surfaces where the potential is constant.
c. Equipotential surfaces for a uniform electric field are parallel and equidistant from each other.
d. Electric field is always perpendicular to an equipotential surface.
67023.sol:
The work done in moving a charge $q$ from point A to point B is given by $W = q(V_B - V_A)$.

For an equipotential surface, the potential is constant everywhere, which means $V_A = V_B$.

Substituting this into the work equation gives $W = q(0) = 0$.

Statement a claims that the work done to move a charge on an equipotential surface is not zero, which is incorrect.

Statements b, c, and d describe standard properties of equipotential surfaces and electric fields, and are all true.

Answer: a

68143.subject: Physics
68143.text: Under isothermal conditions, two soap bubbles of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ coalesce to form a big drop. The radius of the big drop is
68143.sol:
The radius $R$ of a large soap bubble formed from the coalescence of two bubbles with radii $r_1 and r_2$ under isothermal conditions can be determined by conserving the total number of moles of gas.

Given that $PV = nRT$ and assuming isothermal conditions, the conservation equation becomes $P_f V_f = P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2$.
For soap bubbles, the internal pressure is $P = P_{atm} + \frac{4T}{r}$, and the volume is $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.

Substituting yields:
$\left(P_{atm} + \frac{4T}{R}\right) \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \left(P_{atm} + \frac{4T}{r_1}\right) \frac{4}{3}\pi r_1^3 + \left(P_{atm} + \frac{4T}{r_2}\right) \frac{4}{3}\pi r_2^3$.

Assuming $P_{atm}$ is negligible compared to the pressure due to surface tension, the equation simplifies to $0 = 4T(r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2)$.
Since $4T \neq 0$, it follows that $R^2 = r_1^2 + r_2^2$.

Thus, $R = \left(r_1^2 + r_2^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$, which corresponds to option C.

69956.text: A monoatomic ideal gas, initially at temperature $T_1$ is enclosed in a cylinder fitted with massless, frictionless piston. By releasing the piston suddenly, the gas is allowed to expand adiabatically to a temperature $T_2$. If $L_1 and L_2$ are the lengths of the gas columns before and after expansion respectively, then $\left(T_2 / T_1\right)$ is given by
69956.sol:
The adiabatic relation for an ideal gas is $TV^{\gamma-1} = \text{constant}$, where $\gamma = C_p/C_v$. For a monoatomic gas, $\gamma = 5/3$ and thus $\gamma - 1 = 2/3$.

Since $T_1V_1^{2/3} = T_2V_2^{2/3}$, the temperature ratio is $\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{2/3}$.

With constant cross-sectional area, volume is proportional to length: $V \propto L$. Therefore, $\frac{V_1}{V_2} = \frac{L_1}{L_2}$ and $\frac{T_2}{T_1} = \left(\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right)^{2/3}$.

This corresponds to option C.

Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by an emotional aversion to food and an obsessive desire to lose weight.

Amnesia refers to the partial or total loss of memory.

71607.subject: Chemistry
71607.text: Identify A, B and C in following reaction when phenol is treated with chloroform in presence of NaOH?
71607.sol:
The given reaction is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

Chloroform reacts with aqueous $NaOH$ to generate dichlorocarbene ($:CCl_2$), which acts as an electrophile. Phenol is converted to the more reactive phenoxide ion by $NaOH$.

The phenoxide ion attacks the dichlorocarbene at the ortho position. After proton transfer and rearomatization, the intermediate [A] formed is sodium 2-(dichloromethyl)phenolate. Its structure has an $-ONa$ group and a $-CHCl_2$ group at ortho positions on the benzene ring.

The $-CHCl_2$ group in intermediate [A] undergoes alkaline hydrolysis with $NaOH$ to form an unstable gem-diol, which immediately loses a water molecule to form an aldehyde group ($-CHO$). This gives intermediate [B], which is sodium 2-formylphenolate (having $-ONa$ and $-CHO$ groups).

Finally, acidification of [B] with $H_3O^+$ protonates the phenoxide oxygen to yield the final product [C], salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde).

Comparing these structures with the given options, the first option correctly identifies [A], [B], and [C].

Answer:

72103.subject: Physics
72103.text: The ratio of angular frequency (\omega$) of an electron to the total energy ( E) of an electron in the first orbit of hydrogen atom is (h$ is the Plank's constant)
72103.sol:
The total energy of an electron in an orbit is given by $E = - \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$.

The angular frequency is $\omega = \dfrac{v}{r}$, which gives $v = \omega r$.

Substituting $v$ in the energy expression:

$E = - \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 r^2$

The ratio of angular frequency to total energy is:

$\dfrac{\omega}{E} = \dfrac{\omega}{- \dfrac{1}{2} m \omega^2 r^2} = \dfrac{-2}{m \omega r^2}$

From Bohr's quantization rule for angular momentum:

$m v r = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

$m \omega r^2 = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

For the first orbit of the hydrogen atom, $n = 1$:

$m \omega r^2 = \dfrac{h}{2\pi}$

Substituting this value in the ratio expression:

$\dfrac{\omega}{E} = \dfrac{-2}{\dfrac{h}{2\pi}} = -\dfrac{4\pi}{h}$

Answer: $- 4\pi / h$

72143.subject: Physics
72143.text: In a Wheatstone's metre bridge, resistances $R$ and $S$ are connected in left and right gap, null point is obtained as $l$. After interchanging the resistances in the gaps, null point shifts to the left by $20$ cm. If the series resistance of $R$ and $S$ is $2\ \text{k}\Omega$, then the value of resistance $R$ is
72143.sol:
For a metre bridge, the balancing condition with resistances $R$ and $S$ in the left and right gaps respectively is given by:

$\dfrac{R}{S} = \dfrac{l}{100 - l}$

When the resistances are interchanged, the new balancing length becomes $100 - l$. It is given that the null point shifts to the left by $20\ \text{cm}$, so the new balancing length is $l - 20$.

Equating the two expressions for the new balancing length:

$100 - l = l - 20$

$2l = 120 \Rightarrow l = 60\ \text{cm}$

Substituting $l = 60\ \text{cm}$ into the initial balancing condition:

$\dfrac{R}{S} = \dfrac{60}{100 - 60} = \dfrac{60}{40} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$\Rightarrow S = \dfrac{2}{3}R$

It is given that the series combination of $R$ and $S$ is $2\ \text{k}\Omega = 2000\ \Omega$.

$R + S = 2000$

$R + \dfrac{2}{3}R = 2000$

$\dfrac{5R}{3} = 2000$

$R = 2000 \times \dfrac{3}{5} = 1200\ \Omega$

Answer: $1200\ \Omega$

72314.subject: Physics
72314.text: A simple pendulum oscillating in air has a period of $\sqrt{3} second. If it is immersed in a non-viscous liquid, having density \rho = \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is the density of the material of the bob, the new period is $2$ second. The value of $x$ is
72314.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum in air is given by:

$T_1 = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}} = \sqrt{3}$

When immersed in a liquid, the effective acceleration due to gravity becomes:

$g_{eff} = g \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho}{\sigma}\right)

The new time period is:

$ T_2 = 2$\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g_{eff}}} =2$

Taking the ratio of the two time periods:

$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} =\sqrt{\dfrac{g}{g_{eff}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{\rho}{\sigma}$}}

Substituting the given values $ T_1 = \sqrt{3}, $ T_2 = 2$, and $\rho = $\dfrac{\sigma}{x}:

\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{x}}}

Squaring both sides:

\dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{x}}

1 - \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{3}{4}

\dfrac{1}{x} =1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}

$ x = 4$

Answer: 4$

72399.subject: Physics
72399.text: A resistance thermometer has resistance $95\ \Omega$ at the ice point and $140\ \Omega$ at the steam point. The resistance obtained if the actual temperature is $30^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ is
72399.sol:
Using the formula for temperature on the resistance scale:

$t = \dfrac{R_t - R_0}{R_{100} - R_0} \times 100$

Given $R_0 = 95\ \Omega$, $R_{100} = 140\ \Omega$, and $t = 30^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Substituting the values:

$30 = \dfrac{R_t - 95}{140 - 95} \times 100$

$30 = \dfrac{R_t - 95}{45} \times 100$

$R_t - 95 = \dfrac{30 \times 45}{100}$

$R_t - 95 = 13.5$

$R_t = 95 + 13.5 = 108.5\ \Omega$

Answer: $108.5\ \Omega$

72506.text: A string fixed at both the ends, forms a standing wave with node separation of $5\ \text{cm}$. If the velocity of the wave on the string is $2\ \text{m/s}$, then the frequency of vibration of the string is
72506.sol:
The distance between two consecutive nodes in a standing wave is $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$.

Given that the node separation is $5\ \text{cm}$, we have:

$\dfrac{\lambda}{2} = 5\ \text{cm} = 0.05\ \text{m}$

$\lambda = 0.1\ \text{m}$

The velocity of the wave is given as $v = 2\ \text{m/s}$.

The frequency of vibration $f$ is related to the wave velocity and wavelength by the formula:

$f = \dfrac{v}{\lambda}$

Substituting the values:

$f = \dfrac{2}{0.1} = 20\ \text{Hz}$

Answer: $20\ \text{Hz}$

72513.subject: Physics
72513.text: A hollow pipe of length 0.8 m is closed at one end. At its open end a 0.5 m long uniform string is vibrating in fourth harmonic, and it resonates with the fundamental frequency of the pipe. If the tension in the wire is 50 N and the speed of sound is 320 m/s, the mass of string is
72513.sol:
The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe of length $L_p$ is given by $f_p = \dfrac{v}{4 L_p}$.

Substituting the given values, $v = 320$ m/s and $L_p = 0.8$ m:

$f_p = \dfrac{320}{4 \times 0.8} = \dfrac{320}{3.2} = 100$ Hz

The frequency of the fourth harmonic of a string of length $L_s$ fixed at both ends is given by $f_s = \dfrac{4}{2 L_s} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $T$ is the tension and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

Given that the string resonates with the fundamental frequency of the pipe, $f_s = f_p = 100$ Hz.

Substituting $L_s = 0.5$ m and $T = 50$ N:

$100 = \dfrac{4}{2 \times 0.5} \sqrt{\dfrac{50}{\mu}}$

$100 = 4 \sqrt{\dfrac{50}{\mu}}$

$25 = \sqrt{\dfrac{50}{\mu}}$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$625 = \dfrac{50}{\mu} \Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{50}{625} = 0.08$ kg/m

The mass of the string $m$ is the product of its linear mass density and length:

$m = \mu L_s = 0.08 \times 0.5 = 0.04$ kg

Converting to grams, $m = 40$ g.

Answer: $40$ g

75114.text:
Consider the following offices:
I. The Vice President of India
II. The Governors within their respective States
III. The Prime Minister of India
IV. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Which one of the following options represents the correct order of these offices for ceremonial occasions in the Table of Precedence as approved by the President of India?
75114.sol:
According to the Table of Precedence of the Republic of India, the order of precedence is as follows:

Rank $1$: President of India
Rank $2$: Vice President of India (I)
Rank $3$: Prime Minister of India (III)
Rank $4$: Governors of States within their respective States (II)
Rank $5$: Former Presidents
Rank $5$A: Deputy Prime Minister
Rank $6$: Chief Justice of India, Speaker of the Lok Sabha (IV)

Thus, the correct order of precedence for the given offices is Vice President of India, Prime Minister of India, Governors within their respective States, and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

The correct sequence is I, III, II, IV.

Answer: I, III, II, IV

If $M^{\text{T}}$ is the transpose of a $2\times2$ matrix $M$, then which of the following is/are correct ?
I. $|M+M^{\text{T}}|=|M|+|M^{\text{T}}|$ if $M$ is symmetric.
II. $|M+M^{\text{T}}|=0$ if $M$ is anti-symmetric.
Select the answer using the code given below :
77710.sol:
For Statement I:

If $M$ is a symmetric matrix of order $2 \times 2$, then $M^{\text{T}} = M$.

$|M+M^{\text{T}}| = |2M| = 2^2|M| = 4|M|$

$|M| + |M^{\text{T}}| = |M| + |M| = 2|M|$

Since $4|M| \neq 2|M|$ for all symmetric matrices, Statement I is incorrect.

For Statement II:

If $M$ is an anti-symmetric matrix, then $M^{\text{T}} = -M$.

$M+M^{\text{T}} = M - M = O$

$|M+M^{\text{T}}| = |O| = 0$

Statement II is correct.

Answer: II only

78521.subject: Mathematics
78521.text: The arithmetic mean of 100 observations is 50. If 5 is subtracted from each observation and then divided by 20, then what is the new arithmetic mean?
78521.sol:
Let the original observations be $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{100}$.

The original arithmetic mean is $\bar{x} = 50$.

The new observations are given by $y_i = \dfrac{x_i - 5}{20}$.

Using the property of arithmetic mean, if each observation is subjected to a linear transformation $y_i = a x_i + b$, the new mean is $\bar{y} = a \bar{x} + b$.

Therefore, the new mean is $\bar{y} = \dfrac{\bar{x} - 5}{20}$.

Substituting $\bar{x} = 50$, we get $\bar{y} = \dfrac{50 - 5}{20} = \dfrac{45}{20} = 2.25$.

Answer: $2.25$

79812.subject: Botany
79812.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Chromosomes are fully condensed at the end of prophase I.
Statement II : Meiosis I resembles mitosis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
79812.sol:
According to the NCERT, diakinesis is the final stage of meiotic prophase I. During this phase, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis. In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis because it involves the separation of sister chromatids. Meiosis I is a reductional division where homologous chromosomes separate. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false

79838.text: The fruit fly has $8$ chromosomes $( 2n )$ in each cell. During the interphase of mitosis if the number of chromosomes at ${G}_{1}$ phase is $8 .$ What would be the number of chromosomes after the S phase?
79838.sol:
The number of chromosomes remains the same after S-phase, but the amount of DNA becomes double.

S phase is the phase of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, occurring between the G1 phase and G2 phase. Since accurate duplication of the genome is critical to successful cell division, the processes that occur during S-phase are tightly regulated and widely conserved.

82133.subject: Physics
82133.text: The peak value of an alternating current is $5$ A and frequency is $60$ Hz. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value ?
82133.sol:
The alternating current is given by $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

The time taken to reach the peak value from zero corresponds to a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

$\omega t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$2 \pi f t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$t = \dfrac{1}{4f}$

Given $f = 60$ Hz, we get:

$t = \dfrac{1}{4 \times 60} = \dfrac{1}{240}$ s.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{240}$ s

82661.subject: Physics
82661.text:
A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius $R$, having uniform positive charge density $\rho$, as shown in the figure. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by $A$ and $B$ at distances $2R$ and $3R$ respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is $\dfrac{\rho R^2}{n\epsilon_0}$. The value of $n$ is :
($\epsilon_0$ is the permittivity of vacuum)
82661.sol:
Since the electrostatic field is conservative, the work done in moving a charge depends only on the potential difference between the initial and final positions, regardless of the path taken.

The electric potential $V(r)$ at a distance $r$ ($r \ge R$) from the centre of a uniformly charged solid sphere of radius $R$ and charge density $\rho$ is given by:
$V(r) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{r}$

The total charge $Q$ of the sphere is:
$Q = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho$

Substituting $Q$ into the potential formula, we get:
$V(r) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho}{r} = \dfrac{\rho R^3}{3\epsilon_0 r}$

The initial position $A$ is at a distance $r_A = 2R$ from the centre. The potential at $A$ is:
$V_A = \dfrac{\rho R^3}{3\epsilon_0 (2R)} = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{6\epsilon_0}$

The final position $B$ is at a distance $r_B = 3R$ from the centre. The potential at $B$ is:
$V_B = \dfrac{\rho R^3}{3\epsilon_0 (3R)} = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{9\epsilon_0}$

The work done by the external agent in moving a unit positive charge ($q = 1$) slowly from $A$ to $B$ is equal to the change in its potential energy:
$W = q(V_B - V_A) = 1 \times \left( \dfrac{\rho R^2}{9\epsilon_0} - \dfrac{\rho R^2}{6\epsilon_0} \right)$

$W = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{\epsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{2 - 3}{18} \right) = -\dfrac{\rho R^2}{18\epsilon_0}$

The magnitude of the total work done is:
$|W| = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{18\epsilon_0}$

Comparing this with the given expression $\dfrac{\rho R^2}{n\epsilon_0}$, we find:
$n = 18$

Answer: $18$

83337.subject: Physics
83337.text: Consider three media $P$, $Q$ and $R$ with refractive indices $1$, $1.25$, and $1.5$, respectively. The medium $Q$ having a thickness of $5$ cm is placed between extended media $P$ and $R$ as shown in the figure. An object $O$ is placed at the center of medium $Q$. If viewed from medium $P$ near the normal direction, the apparent depth of $O$ is $h_1$. For similar observation from medium $R$, the apparent depth is $h_2$. The value of $|h_1-h_2|$, in cm, is :
83337.sol:
The object $O$ is placed at the center of medium $Q$, which has a thickness of $5\text{ cm}$. Therefore, the actual depth of the object from both the $P-Q$ interface and the $Q-R$ interface is:

$d = \dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5\text{ cm}$

The formula for apparent depth when viewed from a medium of refractive index $n_{\text{observer}}$ into a medium of refractive index $n_{\text{object}}$ is given by:

$h_{\text{app}} = d \times \dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_{\text{object}}}$

When viewed from medium $P$ ($n_P = 1$), the apparent depth $h_1$ of the object in medium $Q$ ($n_Q = 1.25$) is:

$h_1 = 2.5 \times \dfrac{n_P}{n_Q} = 2.5 \times \dfrac{1}{1.25} = 2.5 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 2\text{ cm}$

When viewed from medium $R$ ($n_R = 1.5$), the apparent depth $h_2$ of the object in medium $Q$ ($n_Q = 1.25$) is:

$h_2 = 2.5 \times \dfrac{n_R}{n_Q} = 2.5 \times \dfrac{1.5}{1.25} = 2.5 \times \dfrac{6/4}{5/4} = 2.5 \times \dfrac{6}{5} = 3\text{ cm}$

We need to find the value of $|h_1 - h_2|$:

86940.subject: Physics
86940.text: The critical electric field required to produce electron-positron pairs depends on the physical constants $h$, $c$, $m_e$ and $e$. Use dimensional analysis and assume that the dimensionless coefficient is of order one. The magnitude of the critical electric field, in SI units, is of the order
86940.sol:
Let the critical electric field be expressed as $E = h^\alpha c^\beta m_e^\gamma e^\delta$.

The dimensional formulas for the given quantities are:
$[E] = M L T^{-3} A^{-1}$
$[h] = M L^2 T^{-1}$
$[c] = L T^{-1}$
$[m_e] = M$
$[e] = A T$

Substituting these dimensions into the assumed relation:
$M L T^{-3} A^{-1} = (M L^2 T^{-1})^\alpha (L T^{-1})^\beta M^\gamma (A T)^\delta$
$M L T^{-3} A^{-1} = M^{\alpha+\gamma} L^{2\alpha+\beta} T^{-\alpha-\beta+\delta} A^\delta$

Equating the powers of the fundamental dimensions on both sides:
For $A$: $\delta = -1$
For $M$: $\alpha + \gamma = 1$
For $L$: $2\alpha + \beta = 1$
For $T$: $-\alpha - \beta + \delta = -3 \Rightarrow -\alpha - \beta - 1 = -3 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 2$

Solving the system of equations:
Subtracting $\alpha + \beta = 2$ from $2\alpha + \beta = 1$, we get $\alpha = -1$.
Substituting $\alpha = -1$ into $\alpha + \beta = 2$, we get $\beta = 3$.
Substituting $\alpha = -1$ into $\alpha + \gamma = 1$, we get $\gamma = 2$.

Thus, the expression for the critical electric field is:
$E = \dfrac{m_e^2 c^3}{e h}$

Substituting the standard SI values of the constants:
$m_e \approx 9.1 \times 10^{-31}$ kg
$c \approx 3 \times 10^8$ m/s
$e \approx 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C
$h \approx 6.63 \times 10^{-34}$ J s

$E \approx \dfrac{(9.1 \times 10^{-31})^2 \times (3 \times 10^8)^3}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 6.63 \times 10^{-34}}$

$E \approx \dfrac{82.81 \times 10^{-62} \times 27 \times 10^{24}}{10.6 \times 10^{-53}}$

$E \approx \dfrac{2236 \times 10^{-38}}{10.6 \times 10^{-53}} \approx 211 \times 10^{15} \approx 2.1 \times 10^{17}$ V/m

If we use the reduced Planck constant $\hbar = \dfrac{h}{2\pi} \approx 1.05 \times 10^{-34}$ J s (which is standard for the Schwinger limit in quantum electrodynamics):
$E = \dfrac{m_e^2 c^3}{e \hbar} \approx \dfrac{2236 \times 10^{-38}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1.05 \times 10^{-34}} \approx 1.3 \times 10^{18}$ V/m

In either case, the magnitude of the critical electric field is of the order of $10^{18}$ V/m.

Answer: $10^{18}$

91811.subject: Mathematics
91811.text: Let ${X}_{1}, {X}_{2}, {X}_{3} . . . .$ are in arithmetic progression with a common difference equal to $d$ which is a two digit natural number. ${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}, {y}_{3} . . . .$ are in geometric progression with common ratio equal to $16$ . If the arithmetic mean of ${X}_{6}, {X}_{7} . . . . {X}_{n + 5}$ is equal to the arithmetic mean of ${y}_{P + 1}, {y}_{P + 2} . . . . {y}_{P + n}$, then $d$ is equal to
91811.sol:
Mean $\left({X}_{1}, {X}_{2} \ldots {X}_{n}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{n}{2}\left[2{X}_{1} + \left(n - 1\right)d\right]}{n} = 5$
Mean of $\left({y}_{1}, {y}_{2} . . . . {y}_{n}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{{y}_{1}\left({16}^{n} - 1\right)}{15}}{n} = 5$
$2{X}_{1} + \left(n - 1\right)d = 10$ … $\left(1\right)$
${y}_{1}\left({16}^{n} - 1\right) = 75n$ … $\left(2\right)$
Mean of $\left({X}_{6}, {X}_{7} . . . . {X}_{n + 5}\right) =$ Mean of $\left({y}_{P + 1}, {y}_{P + 2}, {y}_{P + n}\right)$
$\dfrac{\dfrac{n}{2}\left[2{X}_{6} + \left(n - 1\right)d\right]}{n} = \dfrac{{y}_{P + 1}\left({16}^{n} - 1\right)}{15n} = \dfrac{{y}_{1}{16}^{P}\left({16}^{n} - 1\right)}{15n}$
${X}_{6} + \left(\dfrac{n - 1}{2}\right)d = \dfrac{{16}^{P}\left(75n\right)}{15n} = 5 \times {16}^{P}$
${X}_{1} + 5d + \left(\dfrac{n - 1}{2}\right)d = 5 \times {16}^{P}$
$5 - \left(\dfrac{n - 1}{2}\right)d + 5d + \left(\dfrac{n - 1}{2}\right)d = 5 \times {16}^{P} ⇒ d = {16}^{P} - 1$
$∵ d$ is $2$ digit natural number $⇒ P = 1, d = 15$

92665.text: A ball is dropped from a height $h$ on a floor. The coefficient of restitution for the collision between the ball and the floor is $e$. The total distance covered by the ball before it comes to the rest.
92665.sol:
Height achieved in $n^{th}$ collision is given by

${h}_{n} = e^{2n}h$
Distance covered in first collision = $h$,

Distance covered in ${2}^{nd}$ collision = $2e^{2}h$, and so on.

Total distance covered by the ball before it comes to rest:

$s = h + 2e^{2}h + 2e^{4}h +......$

$⇒ s = h \left[1 + \left(2e^{2} + 2e^{4} + 2e^{6} +......\right)\right]$

from the sum of infinite geometric progression:

$⇒ s = h \left[1 + \dfrac{2e^{2}}{1 - e^{2}}\right]$

$⇒ s = h \left[\dfrac{1 + e^{2}}{1 - e^{2}}\right]$

94666.subject: Physics
94666.text: Diagram shows the variation of internal energy $( U )$ with the pressure $( P )$ of $2. 0mole$ gas in cyclic process $abcda$. The temperature of gas at $c$ and $d$ are $300K$ and $500K$, respectively. Calculate the heat absorbed by the gas during the process.
94666.sol:
Change in internal energy for cyclic process $\left(\Delta \text{U}\right) = 0$

For process $\text{a} \to \text{b} \text{,} \left(\text{P} - \text{constant}\right)$

     ${\text{W}}_{\text{a} \to \text{b}} = \text{P} \Delta \text{V} = \text{n} \text{R} \Delta \text{T} = - 4 0 0 \text{R}$

For process $\text{b} \to \text{c} \text{,} \left(\text{T} - \text{constant}\right)$

     ${\text{W}}_{\text{b} \to \text{c}} = nRTln\left(\dfrac{{P}_{i}}{{P}_{f}}\right) = - 2\text{R}\left(300\right)\text{ln}2$

For process $\text{c} \to \text{d} \text{,} \left(\text{P} - \text{constant}\right)$

     ${\text{W}}_{\text{c} \to \text{d}} = \text{P} \Delta \text{V} = \text{nR} \Delta \text{T=} + 400\text{R}$

For process $\text{d} \to \text{a} \text{,} \left(\text{T} - \text{constant}\right)$

     ${\text{W}}_{\text{d} \to \text{a}} = nRTln\left(\dfrac{{P}_{i}}{{P}_{f}}\right) = + 2\text{R}\left(500\right)\text{ln}2$

Net work,

    $\left(\Delta \text{W}\right) = {\text{W}}_{\text{a} \to \text{b}} + {\text{W}}_{\text{b} + \text{c}} + {\text{W}}_{\text{c} \to \text{d}} + {\text{W}}_{\text{d} \to \text{a}}$

      $\Delta \text{W} = 4 0 0 \text{R ln 2}$

$\text{dQ} = \text{dU} + \text{dW}$, first law of thermodynamics

 $\text{dQ} = 4 0 0 \text{R ln 2}$

95014.subject: Physics
95014.text:
A sound source $S$, emitting a sound of frequency $400Hz$ and a receiver $R$ of mass $m$ are at the same point. $R$ is performing SHM with the help of a spring of force constant $K$. At a time $t = 0$, $R$ is at the mean position and moving towards the right, as shown. At the same time, the source starts moving away from $R$ with some acceleration $a$. The frequency registered by the receiver at a time $t = 10s$ is $250Hz$. What is the time (in seconds) at which the corresponding registered frequency of $250Hz$ was emitted by the source?
[Given that $\dfrac{m}{K} = \dfrac{25}{{\pi}^{2}}$ and amplitude of oscillation $= \dfrac{100}{\pi}m$, ${v}_{sound} = 320m{s}^{- 1}$]
95014.sol:
The time period of oscillation $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{K}} = 10s$

So at t = 10 s, the receiver passes through mean position towards the right with a speed

${v}_{R} = A\omega = \dfrac{100}{\pi} \times \dfrac{\pi}{5} = 20m{s}^{- 1}$

Using doppler’s formula

${f}_{\text{app}} = {f}_{0}\left(\dfrac{v - {v}_{R}}{v + {v}_{S}}\right)$

$250 = 400\left(\dfrac{320 - 20}{320 + {v}_{S}}\right) ⇒ {v}_{S} = 160m{s}^{- 1}$

So the velocity of the source is ${v}_{S} = 160m{s}^{- 1}$ at the time of emission of the wave which was received by the receiver at $t = 10s$

Let's say the time instant when the wave was emitted is $T$, then the distance of the source from the receiver is $\dfrac{1}{2}a{t}^{2}$. This distance is travelled by the wave in a time $10 - T$. So,

$\dfrac{1}{2}a{T}^{2} = v\left(10 - T\right)$

${v}_{s} = aT$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{v}_{s}}{T}{T}^{2} = v\left(10 - T\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times 160 \times T = 320 \times \left(10 - T\right)$

$⇒ T = 40 - 4T$

$⇒ T = 8s$

96415.subject: Botany
96415.text: Which of the following is not true about succession?
options: It is a natural process of change in species structure and community with time
It is a gradual and predictable change
Progressive increase in the amount of living biomass as succession proceeds
Food chain relationship becomes less complex as succession proceeds
96415.sol:
Ecosystem characteristics that change during succession:

i) Change in the diversity of species i.e., some species colonize an area and their populations become more numerous, whereas populations of other species decline and even disappear.
ii) Little diversity to a high degree of diversity i.e., increase in the number of species.
iii) Total biomass increases.
iv) Increase in humus content of the soil.
v) Aquatic or dry conditions to mesic conditions i.e, both Hydrarch and Xerarch succession lead to medium water conditions (mesic), neither too dry (xeric) nor too wet (hydric).
vi) Vegetational changes, in turn, affect food and shelter for various types of animals. Thus, as succession proceeds, the number and types of animals and decomposers also change.

100669.subject: Physics
100669.text: A block of mass $m$ is placed on a frictionless inclined plane making an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. A constant external force of $21 \mathrm{~N}$ is applied on the block directed up the incline. If the block accelerates down the incline at $2 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$, what is the value of $m$? (Take $g = 10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$)
100669.sol:
Let the mass of the block be $m$.

The forces acting on the block along the inclined plane are:
1. The component of its weight acting down the incline: $m g \sin 30^{\circ}$
2. The external force acting up the incline: $F = 21 \mathrm{~N}$

Since the block accelerates down the incline at $a = 2 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$, the net force is directed downwards along the incline.

According to Newton's second law:
$m g \sin 30^{\circ} - F = m a$

Substituting the given values ($g = 10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$, $\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5$):
$m(10)(0.5) - 21 = m(2)$
$5m - 21 = 2m$
$3m = 21$
$m = 7 \mathrm{~kg}$

Note: If the block were accelerating up the incline, the equation would be $F - m g \sin 30^{\circ} = m a$, which would yield $m = 3 \mathrm{~kg}$.

Answer: $7 \mathrm{~kg}$

102141.sol:
Given, that $p \propto T^3$ or $p T^{-3}=\text{ constant } \quad \ldots(i)$
Also for adiabatic process,
$\mathrm{pV}^\gamma=\text{ constant }$
But $p V=R T$ (ideal gas law)
or $V=\frac{R T}{p} \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad p\left(\frac{R T}{p}\right)^\gamma & =\text{ constant } \\ p^{1-\gamma} T^\gamma & =\text{ constant }\end{aligned} \text{ or } \quad p T^{\gamma /(1-\gamma)}=\text{ constant } \quad \ldots(ii)$
Equating Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\frac{\gamma}{1-\gamma}=-3
or \gamma=-3+3 \gamma
or 2 \gamma=3\therefore \gamma=\frac{3}{2}\frac{C_p}{C_V}=\frac{3}{2}$

104091.subject: Physics
104091.text:
The rms voltages across the components of a series LCR circuit are given below:
Resistor ($R$): $16\text{ V}$
Inductor ($L$): $24\text{ V}$
Capacitor ($C$): $12\text{ V}$

The instantaneous current flowing through the circuit is given by the equation $i(t) = 4\sqrt{2} \sin(100\pi t)\text{ A}$. The impedance of the circuit is:
104091.sol:
The rms voltage of the source is calculated using the phasor addition formula:

$V_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$

$V_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{16^2 + (24 - 12)^2} = \sqrt{256 + 144} = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ V}$

The peak current from the given equation $i(t) = 4\sqrt{2} \sin(100\pi t)$ is $I_0 = 4\sqrt{2}\text{ A}$.

The rms current is:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 4\text{ A}$

The impedance of the circuit is:

$Z = \dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}}{I_{\text{rms}}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5\ \Omega$

Answer: $5\ \Omega$

105682.subject: Physics
105682.text: If alpha, beta and gamma rays carry same momentum, which has the longest wavelength?
105682.sol:
On the basis of dual nature of light, Lious de-Broglie suggested that the dual nature is not only of light, but each moving material particle has the dual nature. He assumed a wave to be associated with each moving material particle which is called the matter wave. The wavelength of this wave is determined by the momentum of the particle. If $p$ is the momentum of the particle, the wavelength of the wave associated with it is
$\lambda=\frac{h}{p}$
where $h$ is Planck's constant.
Since, it is given that, alpha, beta and gamma rays carry same momentum, so they will have same wavelength.

114353.subject: Chemistry
114353.text:
Given the standard electrode potentials for gold at $298$ K:
$E^\circ(\text{Au}^{3+}/\text{Au}) = +1.40$ V
$E^\circ(\text{Au}^+/\text{Au}) = +1.69$ V

What is the standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$) for the disproportionation reaction of $\text{Au}^+$?
$3\text{Au}^+ \rightarrow \text{Au}^{3+} + 2\text{Au}$
114353.sol:
The disproportionation reaction is $3\text{Au}^+ \rightarrow \text{Au}^{3+} + 2\text{Au}$.
This involves two half-reactions:
Oxidation: $\text{Au}^+ \rightarrow \text{Au}^{3+} + 2e^-$
Reduction: $\text{Au}^+ + e^- \rightarrow \text{Au}$

First, calculate the standard reduction potential for $\text{Au}^{3+}/\text{Au}^+$:
$\text{Au}^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow \text{Au}$, $E^\circ_1 = +1.40$ V, $\Delta G^\circ_1 = -3F(1.40) = -4.20F$
$\text{Au}^+ + e^- \rightarrow \text{Au}$, $E^\circ_2 = +1.69$ V, $\Delta G^\circ_2 = -1F(1.69) = -1.69F$

The target half-reaction is $\text{Au}^{3+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Au}^+$.
This is obtained by subtracting the second reaction from the first:
$\Delta G^\circ_3 = \Delta G^\circ_1 - \Delta G^\circ_2 = -4.20F - (-1.69F) = -2.51F$
$-2FE^\circ_3 = -2.51F \implies E^\circ_3 = +1.255$ V.
So, $E^\circ(\text{Au}^{3+}/\text{Au}^+) = +1.255$ V.

Now, calculate $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ for the disproportionation:
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ(\text{Au}^+/\text{Au}) - E^\circ(\text{Au}^{3+}/\text{Au}^+)$
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.69 \text{ V} - 1.255 \text{ V} = +0.435$ V.

Answer: $+0.435$ V

114364.subject: Chemistry
114364.text:
The limiting molar conductivities ($\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}$) of some strong electrolytes are given below:

Electrolyte$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ} / \mathrm{S~cm}^2~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
$\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$$90$
$\mathrm{HCl}$$425$
$\mathrm{NaCl}$$115$


If the molar conductivity of a $0.02~\mathrm{mol~L}^{-1}$ solution of acetic acid ($\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$) is $48~\mathrm{S~cm}^2~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, its degree of dissociation is:
114364.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, the limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid ($\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$) can be calculated from the given strong electrolytes:

$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}) = \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CH_3COONa}) + \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}(\mathrm{HCl}) - \Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}(\mathrm{NaCl})$
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}) = 90 + 425 - 115 = 400~\mathrm{S~cm}^2~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

The degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) is the ratio of molar conductivity at a given concentration to the limiting molar conductivity:

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ}}$
$\alpha = \dfrac{48}{400} = 0.12$

Adding all three values incorrectly yields $630$, giving $0.076$. Using only the salt's value yields $0.53$.

Answer: $0.12$

121006.subject: Chemistry
121006.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In proteins, only right-handed helices are observed.
Reason (R): Secondary structure of protein refers to the local folding of the polypeptide chain into structures like helices.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
121006.sol:
According to NCERT, in proteins, only right-handed helices are observed. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

The secondary structure of a protein indeed refers to the local folding of the polypeptide chain, with the $\alpha$-helix being a prominent example. Thus, the Reason is also correct.

However, the general definition of secondary structure does not explain why only right-handed helices are formed (which is due to the stereochemistry of the constituent amino acids). Therefore, both statements are correct, but the Reason is not the correct explanation for the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

121131.subject: Botany
121131.text: According to the paragraph, what was the earliest basis for classifications of organisms?
121131.sol: Hence, characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are the processes that are basic to taxonomy. Taxonomy is not something new. Human beings have always been interested in knowing more and more about the various kinds of organisms, particularly with reference to their own use. In early days, human beings needed to find sources for their basic needs of food, clothing and shelter. Hence, the earliest classifications were based on the ‘uses’ of various organisms. Human beings were, since long, not only interested in knowing more about different kinds of organisms and their diversities, but also the relationships among them. This branch of study was referred to as systematics. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word ‘systema’ which means systematic arrangement of organisms. Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication.

122196.sol: :The common name for members of the phylum that sponges belong to is Porifera. Sponges are generally marine animals and are typically found in marine environments.Choanocytes, also known as collar cells, line the spongocoel and canals in sponges and play a role in water transport. Digestion is intracellular. The body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres. Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite), i.e., eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual. Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation and sexually by formation of gametes. Fertilisation is internal and development is indirect having a larval stage which is morphologically distinct from the adult.

122981.text: A flower is observed to have vexillary aestivation in its corolla. Which of the following combinations of floral symmetry and placentation is most likely to be found in this flower?
122981.sol:
Vexillary aestivation is a characteristic feature of the family Fabaceae (e.g., pea, bean).

Flowers belonging to the family Fabaceae exhibit zygomorphic (bilateral) symmetry. Their gynoecium consists of a monocarpellary, unilocular ovary with marginal placentation.

Actinomorphic symmetry and axile placentation are typically seen in families like Solanaceae and Liliaceae, which do not show vexillary aestivation.

Answer: Zygomorphic symmetry and marginal placentation

122991.subject: Botany
122991.text:
Observe the following floral formula of a plant family (the symbol for sexuality is omitted):

$\oplus \text{ } \text{K}_{(5)} \text{ } \overset{\frown}{\text{C}_{(5)} \text{A}_{5}} \text{ } \underline{\text{G}}_{(2)}$

Read the following statements regarding the morphology of the flower based on this formula:
(A) The flower exhibits actinomorphic symmetry.
(B) The stamens are attached to the perianth, showing an epiphyllous condition.
(C) The gynoecium consists of a superior ovary.
(D) The sepals are free from one another.

How many of the above statements are correct?
122991.sol:
The given floral formula represents the family Solanaceae.

Statement (A) is correct: The symbol $\oplus$ indicates that the flower is actinomorphic (radial symmetry).

Statement (B) is incorrect: The arc over $\text{C}_{(5)}$ and $\text{A}_{5}$ ($\overset{\frown}{\text{C}_{(5)} \text{A}_{5}}$) indicates that the stamens are attached to the petals, which is the epipetalous condition. The epiphyllous condition involves attachment to the perianth ($\text{P}$).

Statement (C) is correct: The line below $\text{G}$ ($\underline{\text{G}}$) indicates a superior ovary.

Statement (D) is incorrect: The brackets around the number of sepals in $\text{K}_{(5)}$ indicate that the sepals are fused (gamosepalous condition), not free.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (C)) are correct.

Answer: Two

123418.subject: Botany
123418.text:
Read the following statements regarding the anatomy of a dorsiventral leaf:

(A) The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis.
(B) The spongy parenchyma is situated adaxially and consists of loosely arranged cells.
(C) The size of vascular bundles is dependent on the size of the veins.
(D) The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves.

How many of the above statements are correct?
123418.sol:
Statement (A) is correct. In a dorsiventral (dicotyledonous) leaf, the lower (abaxial) surface bears more stomata than the upper surface to prevent excessive water loss.

Statement (B) is incorrect. The spongy parenchyma is situated abaxially (below the palisade cells and extending to the lower epidermis), while the palisade parenchyma is placed adaxially.

Statement (C) is correct. The vascular system includes vascular bundles seen in the veins and midrib, and their size is dependent on the size of the veins.

Statement (D) is correct. Dicot leaves exhibit reticulate venation, where the veins vary in thickness.

Therefore, exactly three statements ((A), (C), and (D)) are correct.

Answer: Three

124921.subject: Botany
124921.text: Why do plants not need specialized organs for gas exchange?
options: Each plant part takes care of its own gas-exchange needs
124921.sol: Yes, plants require O2 for respiration to occur and they also give out CO2. Hence, plants have systems in place that ensure the availability of O2. Plants, unlike animals, have no specialized organs for gaseous exchange but they have stomata and lenticels for this purpose. There are several reasons why plants can get along without respiratory organs. First, each plant part takes care of its own gas-exchange needs. There is very little transport of gases from one plant part to another. Second, plants do not present great demands for gas exchange. Roots, stems and leaves respire at rates far lower than animals do. Only during photosynthesis are large volumes of gases exchanged and, each leaf is well adapted to take care of its own needs during these periods. When cells photosynthesize, availability of O2 is not a problem in these cells since O2 is released within the cell

126790.text:
Read the following statement and identify the correct terms for X, Y, and Z.

"A non-protein organic compound (X) is tightly bound to the enzyme protein (Y) to form a complete catalytically active complex (Z)."

X = Prosthetic group, Y = Holoenzyme, Z = Apoenzyme
X = Prosthetic group, Y = Apoenzyme, Z = Holoenzyme
X = Metal ion, Y = Apoenzyme, Z = Holoenzyme
126790.sol:
According to NCERT, prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. Thus, X is a prosthetic group.

The protein portion of the enzyme is called the apoenzyme, making Y the apoenzyme.

The complete, catalytically active enzyme together with its bound cofactor is called the holoenzyme, making Z the holoenzyme.

Coenzymes are also organic but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient. Metal ions are inorganic cofactors.

Answer: X = Prosthetic group, Y = Apoenzyme, Z = Holoenzyme

126812.subject: Botany
126812.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.

Statement II : When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
126812.sol:
Enzymes are basically proteins, except for ribozymes. They show quaternary structures which are stabilised by various types of interactions, like H-bond, disulphide bonds, etc.

  • Enzymes generally function in a narrow range of temperature and pH.
  • Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.
  • An inhibitor is any chemical substance which can stop the enzyme from action.
  • When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. The inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate is an example of this category.

129715.subject: Zoology
129715.text: In a hypothetical mammal, the kidneys possess exclusively cortical nephrons with no juxtamedullary nephrons. Which of the following would be the direct consequence on its excretory system?
options: The vasa recta would be highly reduced or absent, resulting in an inability to produce highly concentrated urine.
The vasa recta would become highly developed in the cortex to compensate for the short loops of Henle.
The counter current mechanism would operate exclusively in the cortex to maintain the medullary osmotic gradient.
The osmotic gradient in the inner medulla would still reach $1200 \text{ mOsmol L}^{-1}$ due to active transport by the collecting duct alone.
129715.sol:
In cortical nephrons, the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla. Furthermore, the vasa recta is absent or highly reduced in these nephrons.

The counter current mechanism, which is responsible for creating and maintaining the high osmolarity of the inner medullary interstitium (up to $1200 \text{ mOsmol L}^{-1}$), strictly relies on the long loops of Henle of juxtamedullary nephrons and the accompanying vasa recta extending deep into the medulla.

Without these structures, the medullary osmotic gradient cannot be established. Consequently, water cannot be efficiently reabsorbed from the collecting duct, leading to an inability to produce highly concentrated urine. The collecting duct alone cannot generate this gradient.

Answer: The vasa recta would be highly reduced or absent, resulting in an inability to produce highly concentrated urine.

129902.subject: Zoology
129902.text: What signals the rhythm centre to make necessary adjustments in the respiratory process?
options: Receptors associated with aortic arch and carotid artery
129902.sol: This is done by the neural system. A specialised centre present in the medulla region of the brain called respiratory rhythm centre is primarily responsible for this regulation. Another centre present in the pons region of the brain called pneumotaxic centre can moderate the functions of the respiratory rhythm centre. Neural signal from this centre can reduce the duration of inspiration and thereby alter the respiratory rate. A chemosensitive area is situated adjacent to the rhythm centre which is highly sensitive to CO2 and hydrogen ions. Increase in these substances can activate this centre, which in turn can signal the rhythm centre to make necessary adjustments in the respiratory process by which these substances can be eliminated. Receptors associated with aortic arch and carotid artery also can recognize changes in CO2 and H+ concentration and send necessary signals to the rhythm centre for remedial actions.

130451.text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the skeletal system that is conserved across almost all mammals, including human beings?

130564.subject: Zoology
130564.text: What is one example of a natural method of contraception?
130564.sol: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected. As chances of fertilisation are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period. Therefore, by abstaining from coitus during this period, conception could be prevented. Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination. Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition. As no medicines or devices are used in these methods, side effects are almost nil. Chances of failure, though, of this method are also high.
